Documentation photograph of an art installation in a museum exhibition hall at night: A huge backlit wall panel glows across most of one wall of the warm, dim museum lobby; one visitor stands to the side.

The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Shot: Camera at chest height, 35mm lens, f/4, square to the panel. The glowing panel fills about 60 percent of the frame width; its soft reflection on the dark floor below; the warm peach soffit across the top of the frame; a dark doorway at the left edge; one visitor small at the right. Framing like a straight, frontal documentation photo: the camera stands square to the work at chest height, the work sits a little left of centre, the warm ceiling band fills the top fifth of the frame and the dark floor the bottom quarter. Visitors appear only as small dark silhouettes, seen from behind against the light, never more than a fraction of the frame; no face or profile shows.

Place: One and the same museum entrance lobby in every image: low ceiling with a deep soffit lit from above in a soft warm peach-salmon glow, smooth warm cream and beige plaster walls, a dark doorway or glass door at the left edge, and a dark polished stone floor that holds a soft blurred reflection of the light. Quiet, after hours, nobody working.

Light: Two lights only: the installation glows a clean, slightly cool white, and the ceiling soffit glows warm peach above; together they light the cream walls in a warm, low, even dimness. Soft contrast, no hard spotlights; the floor reflection is soft and blurred, not mirror sharp.

Palette and grade: Warm and soft: peach and salmon at the ceiling, warm cream and sand walls, deep warm brown-black floor; the glowing face is clean white with the faintest cool tint, so it stands apart from the warm room. Slightly lifted soft blacks. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of an art installation, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, the way an exhibition photographer frames the work, never a tiny object in a big room. It is a real photograph made in camera by an art documentation photographer, not a render. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The space shows small honest signs of use; the design surface itself is new and clean. The glowing surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation, bloom, haze or glow over it.

Design surface: THE WALL PANEL FACE IS PLAIN EVENLY LIT WHITE, glowing bright and clean edge to edge, clearly the brightest thing in the frame yet not blown out, with crisp corners; nothing on it.

Finish: Like a quiet documentation photo of a museum lobby taken on a good camera at high ISO: soft natural grain, gentle highlight roll-off, a little softness at the edges, honest dim exposure. Real and unpolished, never a render.
